title: Christian's Work Portfolio with Healthier Texas

hero.title: How I Designed Campaigns That Drove 40K+ App Installs and Reached 10K Event Attendees
hero.subtitle: Campaign Design for Public Health & Wellness

lede: Healthier Texas (formerly It’s Time Texas) is a statewide public health organization focused on wellness education, digital outreach, and community engagement. My role spanned social campaigns, video content, and visual storytelling across their web and email platforms during a critical phase of digital expansion.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: Healthier Texas runs statewide wellness campaigns that rely on strong visual communication — but in 2020, everything changed. The pandemic halted in-person events, increased urgency for digital outreach, and created a need to show up with clarity, compassion, and flexibility. The creative team needed design that could adapt quickly across platforms while keeping people—not programs—at the center.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: I partnered with Healthier Texas to bring their campaigns to life across digital and physical spaces. From virtual summit branding to campaign videos and wellness app promotions, I created design systems, social content, and storytelling assets that helped inform and engage. Every piece — whether a social graphic or web visual—was made to feel real, human, and actionable, even in uncertain times.

blocks.h: Engaging Texans in Health and Wellness Amidst a Pandemic
p: When the COVID-19 shutdown hit, Healthier Texas (formerly It’s Time Texas) had to reimagine how they showed up for the public — and fast. Within weeks, we launched two digital-first campaigns built to uplift.

I worked to bring these programs to life visually. For Texans Thrive, I helped shape and visualize the website, turning stories of community resilience into a digital experience grounded in warmth and clarity. For Texas Sweats for Pets, I created a full suite of campaign visuals that included social graphics to email headers to paid ad creative — all designed to motivate movement and drive donations.

p.quote: We needed something that felt joyful and human, even at a time when things felt heavy.

p: Together, these campaigns set the tone for how Healthier Texas would engage through the pandemic — a partner.

gallery.title: Texans Thrive Campaign: Designing a Visual Home for Stories of Resilience
gallery.desc:
At the start of the pandemic, Healthier Texas launched Texans Thrive, a statewide storytelling campaign created to connect communities through shared experience. I was tasked with designing the visual identity for the site and all campaign graphics.
I developed a clean, mobile-forward layout anchored by warm photography and user-submitted stories. The goal was to make each story feel personal and immediate—like flipping through a community scrapbook. I also created custom illustrations and call-to-action modules that invited others to share their voices.
The campaign helped position Healthier Texas as a supportive, human-centred brand during a critical time, and built new digital connections between the organization and its audience.

gallery.title: Texas Sweats for Pets: Designing a Campaign that Got Tails Wagging (and People Moving)
gallery.tools: Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Mailchimp, WordPress
gallery.desc:
To re-energize health goals at the start of 2021, Healthier Texas launched Texas Sweats for Pets — a virtual fitness fundraiser encouraging Texans to work out alongside their pets. My role was to lead the visual direction for the campaign and create all key graphic assets.
I developed a playful visual system that used vibrant illustrations and high-energy type to bring warmth and joy to a fully digital experience. From social posts and email headers to web banners and call-to-action buttons, every asset was designed to feel dynamic and fun while communicating clear ways to participate.
This campaign helped strengthen brand recognition and drove strong turnout across web and email, while deepening our partnership with Austin Pets Alive! and increasing awareness around shared public health and animal welfare goals.

gallery.title: Texas Sweats for Pets: Designing a Campaign that Got Tails Wagging (and People Moving)
gallery.tools: Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Mailchimp, WordPress
gallery.desc: This campaign helped strengthen brand recognition and drove strong turnout across web and email, while deepening our partnership with Austin Pets Alive! and increasing awareness around shared public health and animal welfare goals.

blocks.h: Bringing a Statewide Wellness Conference to Life Through Web and Social
p: The Healthier Texas Summit was one of the state’s largest public health events, and in 2020, it had to go fully virtual. That shift brought new creative challenges: how do you design a digital space that still feels connected, energizing, and real?

I led visual design across the Summit experience, from branded banners and speaker promos to a scalable social template system that could flex with every announcement. I leaned into vibrant color and people-first imagery to create a sense of energy, even through a screen. I didn't want to lose the human element just because it wasn’t being held in person this year.
The result was a visual system that carried through pre-event promotion, livestream assets, and post-event recaps — building consistency and excitement across platforms.

gallery.title: Healthier Texas Summit Speaker Highlights
gallery.desc:
To promote the annual Healthier Texas Summit, I developed a speaker spotlight series that blended vibrant visual identity with a sense of professionalism. The portraits feature high-profile keynote guests like Vice Admiral Jerome M. Adams and Dr. Nadine Gracia, both captured in a bold and clean layout designed to stop the scroll while conveying credibility. The subtle use of gradients and textured overlays offered visual warmth while reinforcing trust, aligning with the summit’s mission of public health equity.
This was a powerful way to bring front-and-centre the voices shaping our national dialogue on health.

gallery.title: Healthier Texas Summit General Campaign
gallery.desc:
This set of promotional graphics was created for various stages of the Healthier Texas Summit campaign—from calls for proposals to registration pushes. Designed to work across social, web, and email, the graphics balanced strong visual contrast with clear CTAs and consistent branding. Key speaker headshots were placed front and centre to personalise the event, while modern geometric overlays gave the campaign a tech-forward yet approachable tone.
The goal was to create something as energetic and impactful as the event itself — while making it effortless for viewers to engage.

blocks.h: Branding Work for Healthy Texas Week + General Visual Support
p: Before the pandemic shifted timelines, I had developed the logo and early visuals for Healthy Texas Week, a campaign encouraging healthy eating and movement. While the event was eventually cancelled, the identity laid the groundwork for future brand efforts.
I also created evergreen visual assets for Healthier Texas’s ongoing digital presence: banners, content templates, and social graphics that helped the team stay consistent and responsive.

gallery.title: Healthy Texas Week Logo Design
gallery.desc: Designed to energize a statewide wellness initiative, this logo for 'Healthy Texas Week' combines playful retro typography with a bold blue Texas silhouette to spark visual impact. I created this mark to feel inviting and optimistic — something families and educators could easily rally around. The use of script lettering adds movement and personality, helping the campaign stand out across digital platforms and printed materials. Though the event was ultimately cancelled due to COVID-19, the logo still served as a unifying visual during early campaign rollout.

gallery.title: Digital Banners for Social Awareness Campaigns
gallery.desc: These social banners were part of two core awareness initiatives: a SNAP-funded campaign promoting community health during the pandemic, and a mobile app called 'Teach Healthier,' offering active brain breaks for kids. I focused on bright, diverse illustrations and clean, legible layouts that could connect with both parents and educators scrolling online. These visuals were used across social media, email newsletters, and website banners to help increase visibility and accessibility of our programs.

blocks.h: Visual Design for Statewide Health Initiatives
p: These two programs brought public health to life at scale. One through playful competition, the other through practical training. For the Community Challenge, a wellness app used by tens of thousands across Texas, I created social, web, and app graphics that encouraged participation while staying accessible and inclusive. For the Regional Workshop Series, I designed digital materials and promotional content to support community leaders and educators.

gallery.title: Community Challenge Web Banner
gallery.desc: A promotional banner for the Community Challenge, one of Healthier Texas’ most impactful programs. The design I used features vibrant, high-contrast colors and a custom illustrated walking path to reflect momentum and unity. With a wave-like trail of diverse community members, the visual metaphor communicates collective movement toward better health. This design helped drive registrations during peak campaign periods and aligned with the broader brand update efforts across channels.

gallery.title: Regional Workshop & Social Media Campaigns
gallery.desc: This collection of digital graphics supported multiple Healthier Texas initiatives, including the Regional Workshop Series, Texas Walks, and SNAP-funded outreach. My role involved creating social-friendly visuals with clear, accessible layouts and consistent branding. Illustrations were used to help humanize virtual events and draw attention on social feeds. While each graphic had a unique audience or objective, they all reflected a shared mission: bringing Texans together through health-focused action.

blocks.h: End-to-End Video Production Featuring Public Leaders and Community Partners
p: From interviews with the Mayor of Austin to spotlights on nonprofit partners, I handled video production end-to-end: scripting, filming, editing, and motion. These pieces helped humanize the broader work, offering audiences a direct connection to the people behind the policies and programs.

blocks.h: Photography to Capture Real Moments and Mission Impact
p: Behind the scenes, I captured photography — mostly for the Healthier Texas Summit and community activations to support social posts, blog content, and newsletters. Whether it was a speaker on stage or a team in motion, the goal was always to reflect the real people moving health forward.

title: Christian's Work Portfolio with Partnerships

hero.title: How I Brought QAD Redzone’s Biggest Partnerships to Life Across Web, Video, and Social
hero.subtitle: Cross-Channel Design for Redzone Partnerships

lede: As Redzone partnered with top-tier brands in the manufacturing and CPG space, I supported their collaborative storytelling through design and video. This case study explores how I helped deliver unified, high-impact creative across web, video, and campaign content.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: Redzone’s partner collaborations were high-profile but creatively fragmented. Materials across slides, social, and web lacked consistency, making it difficult to present a unified brand narrative—especially when aligning with partners like Apple or Ferrara.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: I developed co-branded presentations, social graphics, web features, and video content that told a cohesive visual story. The assets respected each partner’s brand while reinforcing Redzone’s identity across internal and public-facing materials.

blocks.h: Delivering Consistent Visual Storytelling Across Redzone’s Most High-Profile Collaborations
p: Redzone’s reach spans hundreds of manufacturing plants, from household brands like Hershey and Tyson to local family-run operations. Every partner deserves to be represented with the same level of care, consistency, and clarity.

This section highlights the design work I led in collaboration with our most recognizable customers. My goal was always to elevate — not overshadow — their story. That meant building creative that felt personal, on-brand, and fully aligned with each company’s tone, whether it was for a social spotlight, co-branded feature, or event asset.

p.quote: More than just customers, but community members.

p: Every project was rooted in a simple but powerful design philosophy: the partner is the hero, Redzone is the enabler. Through thoughtful type choices, smart layout systems, and visual pacing, I created repeatable frameworks that helped Redzone tell big stories with a consistent brand voice — without ever losing the individuality of the teams we were spotlighting.

gallery.title: Customer Testimonials: Web & Social Graphics
gallery.desc: For this set of branded testimonials, I crafted a cohesive visual style that allowed each customer story to shine while maintaining Redzone’s bold, human-first aesthetic. Whether featured in social media posts or embedded in web placements, each graphic highlights tangible results — like a 34% changeover time reduction or the equivalent of a free plant’s worth of capacity. Quotes from frontline leaders at companies like Nestlé Purina, Post Consumer Brands, and Gorilla Glue were paired with brand-aligned photography and data visuals to underscore impact. My goal was to let the customer voices lead, using layout and color to support a message of real transformation.

gallery.title: Apple Presentation: Community Growth Slide
gallery.desc:
This keynote visual was designed to kick off a major manufacturing leadership summit hosted by Apple. I built a minimalist, emotionally resonant slide that paired growth stats with actual frontline workers to reinforce the human impact behind the numbers. I quickly learned working alongside their team, that tuning this with a more stylized illustration concept and shadowing allowed me to tie brand color with cinematic depth of Apple — helping Redzone stand out in a room full of enterprise software presentations.
The presentation was delivered by QAD Redzone's Blake Strickland.

gallery.title: Leading the Way: Women’s History Month Campaign
gallery.desc: To mark Women's History Month and International Women’s Day, I created this graphic to anchor a larger blog and social campaign highlighting the impact of women across Redzone’s customer base. Rather than spotlighting internal employees, we focused on frontline operators and team leads — like Shannon, Mallory, and Mireya, who are driving transformation from the factory floor. I designed this infographic-style piece with a celebratory and empowering tone, pairing each story with their real accomplishments and strong visual presence. The layout was inspired by award spotlights and magazine-style compositions, centering the theme of recognition and visibility.

gallery.title: Apple Presentation: Product Feature Flow
gallery.desc: Created as part of the same Apple-hosted summit deck, this slide walks the viewer through a day in the life of a plant operator using Redzone. Inspired by the gesture-based interface language of Apple’s own marketing, I designed this slide to feel tactile and intentional — placing each feature along the hand’s movement path to mirror real app interaction. It was one of our most memorable slides, connecting software usability with physical intuition.

blocks.h: Visualizing Redzone’s Reach Across Global Production
p: Real people and products moving through the factory floor every day. To tell that story visually, I created two graphics: a 3D vending machine and a top-down conveyor line, each filled with packaging from actual Redzone customers. From PEZ to Carmex, every item on the shelf or belt represents a frontline team, a success story, a culture of progress.

These visuals were used across global ad placements and social activations, acting as a playful but strategic nod to the real-world impact Redzone powers. It’s design in service of something bigger: recognizing that behind every data point is a snack, a spice jar, or a chocolate bar—and behind those, a person doing their best work.

gallery.title: Bringing the Brand to Life Through Familiar Forms
gallery.desc:
To translate the scale and diversity of Redzone’s customer base into something instantly recognizable, I reimagined the traditional vending machine. But instead of snacks, each slot was filled with product package —everything from Cheesecake Factory's delectable dessert to Tyson chicken strips — designed to match real Redzone customers. Every detail, from the glowing Redzone light to the moving assembly line, was tailored to reflect the modern, tech-forward tone of the brand.
This visual became more than a graphic—it served as an activation point across web, social, and event placements. It visually embodies the question: What do all these brands have in common? Redzone. It’s a simple concept with layered meaning: everyday items, backed by extraordinary frontline teams using the same software.

blocks.h: Transforming Partner Relationships into Scroll-Stopping Video Stories
p: Behind every metric is a person. That belief shaped the video content I created for Redzone — shifting the spotlight away from product features and towards the stories of the people using the software every day.

These weren’t scripted testimonials. They were real moments with real workers — from packaging leads and shift supervisors to maintenance techs — speaking in their own words about what Redzone helped them achieve. I helped concept, script, and shape the visual language of these stories, making sure they felt less like corporate PR and more like short-form stories.

Many of these narrative-driven stories were captured on-site or in close partnership with our customer success team, ensuring every message aligned with what mattered most to that plant. Some videos went further — spotlighting frontline transformation, generational impact, or personal growth in leadership roles. These weren’t just about what Redzone does — they were about how it feels to use it.

blocks.h: Supporting Authenticity and Tone by Capturing the Heart of the Frontline
p: When it came to photography, my goal was to tell a story in a single frame — to capture pride, momentum, and the humanity behind manufacturing.

I directed and captured original photography across customer sites and Redzone events, creating a library of images that showcased more than just process — they showed people in their element. Every image reinforced our brand’s shift toward authenticity and emotional resonance.

These photos supported everything from ad campaigns and customer success stories to web and social use. But more importantly, they helped build Redzone’s visual voice: one that said, “We see you. We’re with you. And your work matters.”

I wanted to make sure that most of these works highlighted that real change starts with real people. And when you’re building a brand rooted in trust, showing the frontline matters just as much as showing the software.

title: Christian's Freelance Work Portfolio

hero.title: How I Explored Brand Identity and Creative Storytelling Through Client and Personal Work
hero.subtitle: Beyond the Brief

lede: This collection brings together freelance work, self-directed creative projects, and visual storytelling developed outside of full-time roles. From real client branding needs to personal campaign experiments, each project reflects a different aspect of my design approach — whether that’s refining layout systems, developing voice, or pushing visual identity in new directions.

blocks.h: THE PROBLEM
p: Working within structured brand environments often means playing it safe. I wanted space to explore tone, story, and aesthetic choices that don’t always fit traditional formats — while also taking on freelance projects that challenged me to solve real-world problems within tight timelines and diverse industries.

blocks.h: THE SOLUTION
p: I used this space to build scrollable web layouts, fictional campaigns, identity systems, and brand assets from the ground up. Whether creating for clients, testing bold visuals, or designing just for fun, each piece helped sharpen my instincts, grow my creative range, and expand my ability to translate ideas into clear, visual communication.

blocks.h: Designing for Real Clients with Practical Brand Challenges
p: Outside of in-house roles, I’ve worked with individuals, startups, and causes to craft design that speaks directly to people. Whether it’s helping a new AI brand find its voice through calming, ambient visuals or designing a social campaign to honor a marathon runner's fundraiser for cancer, each freelance project begins the same way: by listening.

Stories made visual. A concert poster that plays with rhythm and typography. A thumbnail that blends interior style with creator personality. A wellness brand that calms with color. Each graphics made with purpose to resonate.
Freelance work gives me the space to explore different tones, tools, and ideas. But the goal is always the same: make it feel honest, human, and emotionally in tune.

gallery.title: Hushhum AI: Marketing Materials
gallery.desc:
Hushum is an AI-powered ambience app designed to help users focus, sleep, and relax through customizable white, pink, and green noise. As part of their launch campaign, I created a series of lifestyle-driven social graphics that would immediately communicate the emotional benefit of the app — not just the feature set.
I leaned into evocative visuals: sun-warmed portraits and fluid shapes that mirror the calming waveforms of ambient sound. Each graphic paired a stylized human moment with a short, lyrical line of copy to invite curiosity and gently explain the product’s key differentiator — the ability to dial into the right kind of noise for your moment.
This project balanced expressive storytelling with brand development, helping position Hushum not as a utility, but as a feeling.

gallery.title: Youtube Thumbnail for Video Series
gallery.desc:
This Youtube thumbnail was created as part of a series exploring modern design principles through a lifestyle lens. In this episode, the creator breaks down “Harsh vs. Soft Features” in mid-century modern interiors — from sculpted wood to clean-lined decor. My challenge was to capture that narrative in a single visual frame.
I built the composition with a layered, editorial feel: warm-toned textures, natural shadows, and a smiling host visually tied to the subject matter. The placement of objects — from the vase to the teak chair — nods to the theme of contrast, while the serif typography lends a tactile, print-like quality that aligns with the aesthetic audience.
A polished but personality-driven thumbnail that reflects the channel’s growing voice — part expert, part creative guide — while drawing in viewers with clear, story-rich cues.

Promotional piece for indie-pop band LANY’s live performance at Stubb’s BBQ in Austin, TX. The challenge was to capture the band’s sleek, modern aesthetic while injecting the visual energy of a live show announcement — all within the vertical, fast-scrolling world of Instagram Stories.
The layered typography gives the illusion of motion and repetition, mimicking the rhythm and buildup of anticipation before a concert. Each line of text bleeds downward with subtle opacity and colour shifts, creating a sense of scale and sound. The hero photo — styled with high contrast and crisp light — plants the viewer eye-level with the band, drawing them into the scene.
This was a great opportunity to experiment with music branding in a way that balanced clarity with fan excitement, and pushed Instagram-native design choices to feel bold, scroll-stopping, and rhythmic.

gallery.title: Boston Marathon Commission
gallery.desc:
This animated graphic was created as a freelance project for a client running the Boston Marathon with Team JAF (Joe Andruzzi Foundation), raising donations in memory of his father who passed away from cancer. More than just a race update, this piece served as a celebration of community, resilience, and purpose — honouring the reason behind every mile.
The design brings together elements of movement and emotion: a photo from the course, donor milestone messaging, and uplifting motion graphics that nod to the impact beyond the pavement. With over $13,000 raised for families facing cancer, it became a shared moment of gratitude and reflection for all who supported.
Projects like this remind me of design’s deeper purpose — not to sell or promote, but to connect. To help visualize what it means when one person’s story moves hundreds to action.

blocks.h: Exploring Form, Flow, and Function Through Web Design
p: One-page scrolls, mock product sites, and UI-driven layouts designed to test storytelling, visual hierarchy, and user interaction across screen sizes. These pieces weren’t just about how things look — they explored how visuals guide attention, how grids flex on mobile, and how design meets curiosity in the first few scrolls.

gallery.title: Fashion E-Commerce Interface
gallery.desc: This fashion interface was designed to feel bold and energetic, with a heavy emphasis on visual identity and shopability. I leaned into a high-contrast palette and oversized grid structure to prioritise product visibility across both web and mobile. Interactive UI components like real-time colour swatches and review stars were included to simulate a full user experience. The mobile translation preserved the same hierarchy, designed to swipe just as smoothly as it scrolls with a card digital wallet style aesthetic.

gallery.title: AI Product Marketplace Interface
gallery.desc: This AI product marketplace mockup explores modularity and visual rhythm within a one-page layout. I wanted each tile to feel like a moment: a headline, a feature, a reason to keep scrolling. The futuristic aesthetic and neon-infused colour palette reinforce the product category, while the layout tests how call-to-actions and product discovery can coexist without overwhelming the user like most sites do.

blocks.h: Pushing Visual Identity and Storytelling Beyond the Brief
p: This section collects experimental work across editorial layouts, digital ads, product brochures, and visual essays—each designed to simulate real-world communication scenarios. From CPG campaigns to corporate report spreads, these projects explore how to lead with structure, reinforce hierarchy, and pair visuals with utility. Whether interactive or printed, each piece aims to feel intentional, elevated, and built with the reader in mind.

gallery.title: Fall in Style: Editorial Promo
gallery.desc:
A promotional concept for a fall fashion campaign, this graphic blends motion-inspired typography with a highly stylized subject image to evoke energy and momentum. The brief I created for myself: capture the feeling of mid-air motion and let the visual lead the storytelling.
I leaned into large, condensed type and a minimalist palette to anchor the dynamic composition. The floating figure — subtly shadowed for depth—emphasizes the seasonal call-to-action while reinforcing the brand’s editorial tone. The result is a sharp, stylish layout that could live in a print magazine or serve as the key art for a digital ad set.

gallery.title: Mercedes-Benz Print Ad Concept
gallery.desc:
This mock full-page ad plays with the tension between mechanical precision and visual minimalism. The headline, “No Adjustments Needed,” became the thematic driver for the layout — evoking a sense of confidence, control, and quality that aligns with the Mercedes-Benz voice.
The chrome detail of the car was shown to feel almost sculptural, while the copy area was purposefully narrow to mirror luxury ad conventions. By keeping whitespace abundant and the design restrained, the piece reads like an intentional pause: an invitation to look closer. This layout was as much about restraint as it was about message delivery.

gallery.title: Mercedes-Benz Banner Ad Suite
gallery.desc:
This series of responsive digital banners was designed to explore how consistent tone and branding can carry across screen sizes and ad placements. Each banner maintains a cohesive design system — same palette, typography, and imagery, but is composed to fit distinct horizontal and vertical formats.
The repeated use of the 'Spread Your Wings' headline paired with overhead convertible views helps establish an elegant, open aesthetic that aligns with the brand’s premium feel. This was a study in balance: keeping things visually captivating while following best practices for digital ad readability and conversion flow.

gallery.title: Future of Robotics Trifold Brochure
gallery.desc:
This informational trifold was built as a conceptual brochure on the future of robotics as we know it — a piece that could live at a conference table or be sent in a mailer. The goal was to design something that felt future-forward while keeping complex information digestible and visually structured.
Each panel was treated like a mini billboard with bold headlines, infographic-style visuals, and staggered content pacing to guide the reader through topics like automation trends, market stats, and industry innovation. The color scheme was intentionally muted to keep it professional, but with enough contrast to keep the visuals engaging.

gallery.title: Go the Mile: Outdoor Promotional Poster
gallery.desc:
This promotional poster draws inspiration from outdoor lifestyle brands and editorial photography. I wanted to create something that felt strong, grounded, and aspirational— so I opted for dramatic imagery paired with oversized type that demands attention.
The headline, 'Go the Mile,' is treated as both a motivational message and a literal call to explore. The muted palette and texture choices reinforce the natural setting, while the minimal copy allows the image to carry emotional weight. It’s a balance of form and function: a cover that reads both at a distance and up close.

This article spread explores a more academic, report-style layout on the topic of digital assistants and emerging AI tools. Designed as part of a advanced marketing project, the layout includes a hierarchy of callouts, subheads, and annotation symbols to guide both quick skimming and deep reading.
The image at the top serves as a subtle thematic anchor, depicting circuitry and digital systems without overwhelming the copy. The design challenge here was clarity: using rhythm, typography, and spacing to help complex content feel more approachable — without compromising credibility.

blocks.h: Foundations in Strategy & Storytelling: Where Research, Insight, and Creative Thinking First Collided...
p: During my time at Texas A&M’s Mays Business School, I was introduced to the intersection of business strategy and human behaviour — and quickly found myself captivated by how design could help shape both. These projects marked my earliest experiments in making ideas feel visual, actionable, and grounded in real-world understanding. Each one tackled a different challenge: from reimagining struggling brands to uncovering behavioural insights in food safety, social platforms, or product design.

The tools were simple. The constraints were tight. But even then, the focus was the same: clarity, resonance, and a user-first mindset. These projects remind me where my creative instincts first shined — and how much can be done with just strategy, storytelling, and some scrappy design.
